Name the known version each record was captured with

Source: R/crt_schema_variant.R
crt_schema_variant.Rd

Looks up each row's schema_version fingerprint among the upstream variants a registered schema lists, and returns the variant's id. A fingerprint the schema does not list comes back NA: a capture shape nobody has recorded yet, which is worth looking at rather than guessing at.

Usage

crt_schema_variant(df, source, file_name)

Arguments

df

A data frame, usually the output of crt_schema_conform().

source

Character. Source family code (e.g. "nge").

file_name

Character. Logical file name (e.g. "form_pscis").

Value

A character vector, one element per row of df: the variant id, or NA where the fingerprint is not listed or is missing.

Details

A fingerprint describes a column set, so on its own it cannot say which build of a form a record came from. Each per-form schema therefore lists its form's known versions as upstream_variants, each with the fingerprint a capture of it produces. That names the version of forms already in the field, with no change to the deployed forms.

crt_schema_conform() reports unlisted fingerprints as a warning of class crate_unknown_fingerprint, for schemas that list any. This function is how to find which rows they were.

Throws when df has no schema_version column, or the schema lists no fingerprints.

See also

crt_schema_fingerprint() for how a fingerprint is computed.

Examples

types <- c(date_time_start = "DATETIME", crew_members = "TEXT")
records <- data.frame(record_id = 1L, schema_version = crt_schema_fingerprint(types))
crt_schema_variant(records, "nge", "form_monitoring_fish_passage")
#> [1] NA
